The Four Costs That Matter

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 23 Sep 2026

In 2013, in a book entitled Too Different For Comfort, Charles and I attempted to look at the major economies through the prism of four important costs: the cost of capital, the cost of labor, the cost of energy and the cost of government. And every now and then, we like to return to this exercise; even if all too often, the results may appear somewhat subjective. After all:Comparing and contrasting the cost of capital between different countries is undeniably the easiest task of the four. One can look at short rates, long rates, the broader shape of yield curves and get a rough sense of the cost of capital in different countries. For example, today, the cost of capital in the US is roughly 350bp to 400bp more expensive than it is in China.
